question.text: Under SEBI AIF Regulations, the books of account of a Category I or Category II AIF must be:

answer.text: Monitored on a daily basis by the auditor for trading positions
Valued in real time by the auditor for unlisted portfolio companies
Audited annually by a qualified auditor
Approved by the auditor as part of the fund manager's investment strategy

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook states that Category I and Category II AIFs are required to have their books of account audited annually by a qualified auditor. Daily trading monitoring, real-time valuation of unlisted portfolio companies, and approval of investment strategy are not audit functions. The Trap: Real-time valuation looks attractive because valuation matters for AIFs, but the auditor reviews valuations for reasonableness as part of the annual audit; valuation itself is performed by the administrator or independent valuer. Note: Based on NISM Series XIX-A workbook pages 85 and 146, which describe the annual audit requirement for Category I/II AIF books of account by a qualified auditor.
